#2252. Vitor Matos must give 21-year-old his Swansea City debut after latest suspension blow: Opinion

Swansea City enter the second international break of the season, 6th in the Championship, but when they return to action, they will be without midfielder Marko Stamenic. He picked up a red card last weekend, and he’ll be suspended for three games.

The Swans have good depth in midfield, so replacing him shouldn’t be an issue. However, it does give the Welsh outfit a great opportunity to give Tom Iorpenda his first start. The 21-year-old joined from Huddersfield Town in the summer but has yet to appear for Vitor Matos’ side.

Swansea City have the youngster under contract until 2029, and there is plenty of time to unlock his talent. However, they cannot let the midfielder stay on the bench all season, and a decision must be made about his short-term future in the next month.

Replacing Stamenic won’t be an easy task for the Swans after his bright campaign so far. The New Zealand international has a successful pass rate of 90.8% and has helped his side keep three clean sheets. Elijah Just and Melker Widell are both options for Matos, but Iorpenda should be his chosen successor after the international break.

Despite no senior appearances this term, the 21-year-old was inspirational during his loan spell at Notts County last season. He made seven assists from an xA of just 4.35 and made 180 defensive contributions across 53 games for the Magpies.

Iorpenda’s downfall in comparison to Stamenic comes through experience. He has yet to feature in the Championship, and a first game back against West Brom will be a tough test. Moreover, starting the youngster would make the Swans a little more vulnerable at the back.

The Englishman operates as a more advanced midfielder, although his 98 tackles last term make him a strong option for Matos to consider. Realistically, if Jay Fulton retains his spot in the starting XI in two weeks, there’s no reason why it can’t be the occasion for the 21-year-old’s first cameo.

If Iorpenda’s lack of game time continues over the winter period, then a loan move away could be the best decision for Swansea City to make. The Swans can’t afford to let the midfielder’s development stagnate, and getting him minutes elsewhere could be beneficial.

The 21-year-old would excel in League One despite few minutes at that level. His dominance in League Two makes a spell there pointless, and plenty of sides in the third tier would welcome the youngster’s talent.

Sooner or later, though, Matos must give an opportunity to Iorpenda. If Swansea City can unlock his potential, then the £1m deal to sign him could turn out to be an exceptional deal.

#2251. Rocchi: "Gli arbitri vanno tutelati, ciò che è successo a Ferrieri Caputi è inaccettabile"

"Che cosa consiglieri a un giovane arbitro? A un giovane direi di fare l’arbitro perché è stata la passione più bella della mia vita. Due, direi di divertirsi perché a me manca tantissimo il campo. Un ragazzino che vuole fare l’arbitro può iniziare una scuola di vita che gli servirà anche fuori". Gianluca Rocchi, ex designatore arbitrale, parla così in occasione del Social Football Summit, in corso di svolgimento all’Allianz Stadium a Torino (qui le dichiarazioni integrali).

"I direttori di gara - continua Rocchi - vanno tutelati: quello che è successo a Maria Sole Ferrieri Caputi è inaccettabile, ad esempio. Tuteliamo gli arbitri perché quei ragazzini potrebbero essere dei vostri figli. I ragazzi vanno tutelati e senza l’arbitro non si può giocare”.

Il rapporto tra designatore e arbitro? “Le difficoltà sono con il gruppo perché è numeroso e gestirlo è complesso. Chi fa il designatore deve fare un percorso breve e faccio mea culpa. Tutto questo si vede anche con gli allenatori dei grandi club. La soddisfazione più grande è quella di aver visto crescere tanti ragazzi che sono impegnati in grandi match europei”.

Come si insegna a convivere con gli errori? “È complesso. L’arbitro bravo è quello che sa reagire al proprio errore. Devi rimanere sempre concentrato e convivere con l’errore. Questo è un consiglio per i giovani”.

#2248. Coppa Italia stile FA Cup, la Serie A approva il bando TV: apertura alle squadre di C

L’assemblea della Lega Calcio Serie A, conclusa da pochi minuti nel contesto del Social Football Summit di Torino, ha approvato all’unanimità il bando per i diritti TV della Coppa Italia, secondo quanto raccolto. Il bando fa riferimento al periodo 2027-2030 della competizione, attualmente trasmessa da Mediaset.

La principale novità, come vi abbiamo anticipato, riguarda l’apertura alle formazioni di Serie C. In particolare, oltre al format attuale (20 squadre di Serie A, 20 di B e 4 di C), nel bando è prevista la possibilità di una formula all’inglese, con la partecipazione di 32 squadre di Serie C, che partirebbero dal primo turno eliminatorio. Non ancora definito il discorso legato a eventuali wild card per le formazioni U23, come pure la possibilità di giocare in casa della squadra meno blasonata, come avviene in FA Cup.

Sarà ora il mercato - nel senso che tutto dipenderà dalle offerte delle TV -, oltre ovviamente al Consiglio Federale (o al Commissario in questo momento), a decidere quale format avrà la Coppa Italia del futuro.

#2247. 23-year-old helping West Brom forget about missing out on £5m summer target: Opinion

West Brom needed to strengthen their right-back position in the summer after Alfie Gilchrist’s struggles, and with George Campbell better suited centrally. WBA pursued a deal for loanee Danny Imray, who had impressed during the second half of the 2025/26 term. However, it was Wrexham who sealed his signature for £5m.

The Baggies ended up recruiting Nolan Galves and Brayann Pereira to strengthen the position ahead of the 2026/27 campaign. Despite a promising start to life at The Hawthorns, Galves sustained an ACL injury that has ruled him out for the remainder of the season.

Pereira stepped in for the injured Frenchman, but his first start couldn’t have gone any worse, with a red card against Derby County. However, since his poor first impression, the 23-year-old has become one of West Brom’s best players. Now, the failure to sign Imray doesn’t look so bad.

Pereira made it just 34 minutes into his first start for West Brom before being sent off. With Galves’ injury, it left James Morrison with a potential dilemma as to whether the Baggies would have an adequate right-back for the season.

However, since returning to the starting XI, the defender has been a mainstay in WBA’s team. His latest game against Millwall was his best display yet, and it’s a positive sign of things to come from the 23-year-old.

Pereira had the most touches in the match with 92 and completed the joint-most dribbles. He also had a pass accuracy of 92% and won all four of his aerial duels. Morrison will be delighted by his turnaround in form, and it is his position to lose now for the rest of the campaign.

Imray was a tough player for West Brom to replace in the summer after his positive loan spell at The Hawthorns. 55.2% of his dribbles were successful last term, and he helped keep seven clean sheets as the West Midlands outfit avoided relegation.

WBA recruited two right-backs for under £2m. This was less than half the amount the former Crystal Palace man was sold for, and Morrison’s side can be pleased with their recruitment. While Galves’ injury is a huge loss to the Baggies, Pereira has helped soften the blow.

The summer arrival has six more successful dribbles than the former loanee and has a better pass rate by 15%. Imray has also found game time limited over the last few weeks at Wrexham. With West Brom 5th in the league and 10 points ahead of the Red Dragons, the 23-year-old could be rethinking his decision.

#2246. Gattuso primo vincitore del Premio Corigliano: cerimonia a Coverciano per il tecnico della Lazio

Il riconoscimento istituito dall’Aiac sarà consegnato da Renzo Ulivieri il 16 novembre, durante la Panchina d’Oro 2026.

Rino Gattuso, attuale tecnico della Lazio, è il primo vincitore del Premio Ernesto Corigliano, istituito dall’Associazione Italiana Allenatori Calcio (Aiac). Secondo quanto riportato da LaC News24, La consegna è prevista il 16 novembre a Coverciano, in occasione della Panchina d’Oro 2026.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Sarà il presidente dell’Aiac, Renzo Ulivieri, a consegnare il riconoscimento a Gattuso. Il tecnico biancoceleste riceverà così la prima assegnazione del premio dedicato a Ernesto Corigliano.

Avvocato cosentino, Corigliano promosse la costituzione dell’Assoallenatori il 19 settembre 1966. Nel sessantesimo anniversario della fondazione, l’Aiac vuole ricordare «il contributo determinante» dato da Corigliano alla nascita di un’organizzazione unitaria degli allenatori, orientata alla tutela della loro professione.

#2245. Gattuso a Lazio Style Channel: “Abbiamo sofferto con il Napoli, ma abbiamo avuto coraggio”

Gennaro Gattuso, allenatore della Lazio, ha parlato ai microfoni di Lazio Style Channel dopo il pari contro il Napoli: “Siamo stati in trincea, potevamo perdere o vincere. Nel primo tempo potevamo fare più gol, nel secondo ci stava la loro reazione. Abbiamo sofferto, poi siamo tornati in partita. Potevamo fare scelte diverse, ho ancora in mente Noslin che calcia con Isaksen solo, la palla di Cancellieri appena entrato, è una mattonella che a Zaccagni piace e potevamo calciare meglio. Nel finale siamo stati là, potevamo attaccare meglio la profondità e siamo stati piatti. Ma mi piace il fatto che i ragazzi fossero delusi a fine partita, anche se non ci deve essere nessuna delusione: hanno dimostrato grande coraggio e mentalità. Siamo stati là con un primo tempo incredibile, poi abbiamo tenuto botta e siamo tornati in partita. Il Napoli ha giocatori forti, che hanno vinto scudetti e Champions. Siamo stati bravi, ci teniamo stretto il punto, ma mi è piaciuta la mentalità. Abbiamo fatto undici gare, ce ne sono ancora tante e dobbiamo dimostrare gara dopo gara. Non guardiamo Inter-Como, dobbiamo capire cosa stiamo facendo e seguire la strada della mentalità. Per un allenatore la cosa più bella è giocare qua a viso aperto, sapevamo che potevamo soffrire qualcosa ma anche loro faticavano a tenerci in alcune fasi. Abbiamo accettato il rischio e mi è piaciuto. Belahyane? È merito suo, ha cambiato atteggiamento. Quando nella vita capisci che la priorità per fare questo lavoro è metterci passione, voglia e appartenenza, allora cresci. Ci abbiamo lavorato, lui l’ha fatto come tanti altri. Taylor ha giocato mezzo zoppo, tanti atteggiamenti positivi per cui essere soddisfatti. Poi vedremo dove arriveremo, ma ci sono tantissime cose positive ed è merito di questi ragazzi”.

#2244. Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

At that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

Cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

Liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré.  Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88)

They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

As usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

Monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

Konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

Nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

It’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’

Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

Monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

Quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

Isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

Much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

Charlie Adam says the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

The referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

Liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

Big cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike

The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

Liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

Liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had quickly restored himself to the vertical.

Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

Tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

Liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe

Liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

The crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

Virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

Liverpool Alisson; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Szoboszlai, Gakpo; Koumaz, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak.

Monaco Hradecky; Vanderson, Dier, Sané, Nazinho; Detourbet, Cabral, Camara, Golovin, Abline, Biereth.

Le 𝐗𝐈 qui débutera cette rencontre face à 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐨𝐥 📋 pic.twitter.com/2cOYRbzUEN

🥳 Feliz aniversário, 𝐅𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐩𝐞 𝐋𝐮𝐢́𝐬! 🎉Notre coach fête aujourd'hui ses 41 ans 🎂 pic.twitter.com/VTd4BQ5rRK

Alisson, Van Dijk and Gakpo return, Ndukwe continues in defence.

The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under new management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

#2242. Inter, Bonny rischia un mese di stop: ecco tutte le partite che salterà

L'Inter nelle prossime settimane dovrà fare i conti con l'assenza di Ange-Yoan Bonny, attaccante che dopo il successo sul Como si è fermato per via di un problema muscolare, saltando così anche la convocazione con la Costa d'Avorio.

"Ange-Yoan Bonny si è sottoposto oggi a esami clinici e strumentali presso l’Istituto Humanitas di Rozzano. Gli esami hanno evidenziato un risentimento muscolare ai flessori della coscia destra", si legge nel comunicato nerazzurro. Secondo Sky, per il giocatore è previsto uno stop compreso fra le 3 e le 4 settimane, con l'Inter che proverà a recuperarlo per inizio dicembre. Ma tutto dipenderà ovviamente dall'evoluzione del percorso di guarigione.

Le partite che salterà sicuramente Bonny Atalanta-Inter, domenica 22 novembre, Serie A Inter-Stoccarda, mercoledì 25 novembre, Champions League Inter-Genoa, sabato 28 novembre, Serie A

Le successive sfide restano in dubbio: l'1 dicembre ancora Inter-Genoa, questa volta di Coppa Italia, il 5 dicembre Frosinone-Inter, mentre il 9 dicembre ecco Borussia Dortmund-Inter in Champions League. Tre gare in cui Chivu spera di poter tornare ad avere a disposizione l'attaccante.

#2241. Key Birmingham City player attracts new transfer interest with Premier League club keen

Birmingham City sit top of the Championship table after 15 games, and one man who has been ever-present is centre-back Phil Neumann. The BCFC star has played all 1,350 minutes of league football this season, and according to reports in Germany, his performances are drawing attention from a higher level.

Sky Sports Germany states that Neumann is of interest to Premier League side Nottingham Forest and Fiorentina of Serie A. There is a chance the Blues defender could jump to a higher level as soon as the winter transfer window.

Chris Davies and co will surely be adamant that a player as key as Neumann does not leave during a push for promotion from the Championship. The 29-year-old signed a three-year deal upon arrival in 2025, so his current contract runs until 2028.

Neumann joined Birmingham City for their step up to Championship football after signing a pre-contract deal in January 2025. He took a bit of time to settle into the Blues side as Davies worked out his preferred centre-back pairing, but a strong end to the 2025/26 season set the German up well for the new campaign.

The City defender has been nigh-on undroppable this term, hence why he has played every minute of all 15 Championship games so far. Across all competitions, the only game Neumann didn’t start ended in a 6-1 loss to Brentford in the Carabao Cup.

Neumann has been one of the Championship’s best centre-backs this season, as displayed by FotMob‘s dataset. Compared to his divisional counterparts, the BCFC ranks in the top 5% for duels won (98), touches in the opposition box (32), defensive contributions (181), tackles (25), interceptions (26) and clearances (115).

Neumann is a powerful and commanding aerial presence and dependable in possession. His partnership with Christoph Klarer is providing the foundation for the Blues to be bolder going forward.

Birmingham City’s trajectory and their ambitions should be enough to fend off interest in Neumann in January. If his head is turned and a big enough bid comes in, that could change things, but the Blues are certainly under no pressure to sell and he appears to be happy on and off the pitch.

Beyond then, however, keeping Neumann will be down to winning promotion. The German has proven himself at Championship level and if the opportunity is there, he will be determined to show he can cut it in top-flight football.

Neumann has previously expressed an interest in returning to the Bundesliga. Nottingham Forest and Fiorentina make for attractive destinations too though, so time will tell just what 2027 has in store for the BCFC star.

#2239. Juventus-Lazio, Daspo per sette tifosi dopo l’aggressione allo Stadium

I provvedimenti durano da uno a cinque anni; l’episodio nel settore Est aveva fermato la partita per circa due minuti.

Sette tifosi juventini hanno ricevuto un Daspo per l’aggressione a due spettatori stranieri durante Juventus-Lazio del 18 ottobre all’Allianz Stadium. Secondo quanto riportato da SportMediaset, I provvedimenti, della durata compresa tra uno e cinque anni, sono stati emessi dal questore di Torino, Massimo Gambino. SportMediaset riferisce che per uno dei sette è stato disposto anche l’obbligo di firma.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

L’episodio è avvenuto nel primo anello del settore Est. L’incontro si era interrotto per circa due minuti a causa di quanto accaduto sugli spalti.

Secondo la ricostruzione della polizia, i sette tifosi si trovavano in posti diversi da quelli assegnati. I due spettatori avevano chiesto di poter occupare i propri seggiolini. Il gruppo si era dapprima opposto e, dopo averli fatti sedere, li aveva aggrediti.

#2237. Kim Hellberg issues emphatic response to Crystal Palace links and questions over Middlesbrough future

Middlesbrough sit 2nd in the Championship table as they battle for promotion to the Premier League. Boro have spent big on star men like Will Lankshear, but a lot of their success is put down to the work of manager Kim Hellberg.

The Swede’s success has not gone unnoticed either, earning wide praise and drawing interest from elsewhere. Crystal Palace are set to sack Pierre Sage and Hellberg has been named among the contenders, but speaking to Fotbollskanalen, he insisted there is nothing in the rumours and he remains committed to the job at the Riverside Stadium.

“Absolutely nothing, absolutely nothing,” Hellberg said when asked about the interest. “It’s always fun to be on lists if that’s the case, it shows that you’ve done something good. After that, I think it’s mostly talk and for me it’s about doing a damn good job here.”

Hellberg is approaching a year in charge of Middlesbrough, having arrived in late November 2025 after Rob Edwards’ departure to Wolves. There were justified worries when Boro had their boss poached, but the Swede has been quite the hit on Teesside.

His entertaining style of play encourages positional freedom and it makes for a great watch. Most importantly though, it delivers the results needed too.

At 38, Hellberg is one of Europe’s most exciting young bosses and that means interest from the likes of Crystal Palace is inevitable. However, he’s happy at an ambitious club that hopes to match his upward trajectory.

Hellberg is a massive asset for Boro, and they know it. It is why they were willing to back him with expensive deals to sign Lankshear, Ashley Phillips and Radek Vitek, and why players of that calibre were willing to move to the Riverside Stadium.

Hellberg’s comments show he is happy at Middlesbrough and committed to their bid to return to the Premier League. It’s little wonder he’s content – the boss has been heavily backed financially, has a playing squad invested in his ethos on and off the pitch, and has the adoration of the Boro faithful.

However, given his potential in the dugout, the club have to keep progressing to keep him happy. If Hellberg’s progress maintains at this trajectory and Middlesbrough can not match it, opportunities elsewhere will start to become more tempting.

It means promotion is key this season. Boro are on course to achieve that feat as they sit 2nd in the table, but avoiding further heartbreak is a must if Hellberg is to stay committed for the long term.

#2236. Sabatini: “Il Napoli ha giocato le tre partite più spettacolari della stagione”

Il giornalista Sandro Sabatini, attraverso un video pubblicato sul proprio canale YouTube, ha analizzato il pareggio per 1-1 tra Napoli e Lazio: “Le tre partite più belle, spettacolari, ricche di gol, emozioni e occasioni di questa stagione sono state Inter-Napoli 3-2, Napoli-Roma 3-3 e Napoli-Lazio 1-1. Il calcio dominante, propositivo e moderno si è visto in queste tre partite del Napoli, che sono state tra le migliori di un campionato che, magari dopo la sosta, potrà riservare qualche correzione. È proprio il Napoli di Allegri ad augurarsi questa correzione, perché la classifica parla chiaro. Nonostante alcune prestazioni all’altezza della situazione, gli azzurri si ritrovano staccatissimi, intorno al decimo posto, con un divario obiettivamente incolmabile per un’eventuale lotta scudetto e quasi incolmabile persino per il quarto posto. Il calcio è così, è paradossale. Non sempre si riesce a trovare una conferma o una chiave di lettura per qualsiasi partita, a meno che non ci si voglia lasciare guidare dalle ideologie e dai commenti precostituiti, anziché dalle idee e dall’analisi. Fatta questa premessa, Napoli e Lazio hanno pareggiato 1-1 al termine di una partita molto emozionante, spettacolare e combattuta. Il primo tempo è stato maggiormente favorevole alla Lazio, che infatti lo ha concluso in vantaggio per 1-0. Nella ripresa il Napoli ha trovato il pareggio, propiziato da McTominay e Hojlund, con la complicità di Pedraza, autore dell’autogol. Gli azzurri hanno poi costruito altre occasioni, neutralizzate dal portiere. Su tutte, quella clamorosa nel duello faccia a faccia con De Bruyne. Sì, il Napoli nel secondo tempo avrebbe potuto anche vincere, ma la Lazio è una squadra solida, che merita il primo posto in classifica. Gattuso l’ha organizzata benissimo. Mi è piaciuto tantissimo il primo tempo della Lazio, ma anche la gestione degli ultimi dieci minuti, nei quali ha giocato da grande squadra. Bisogna considerare che anche la Lazio, così come il Napoli, ha dovuto fare i conti con assenze importanti. A un certo punto è stata costretta a rinunciare a Sutalo e Nuno Tavares, oltre a dover fare a meno di Zaccagni. Tre assenze pesanti, eppure la Lazio esce dal Maradona tra la soddisfazione dei propri tifosi. I sostenitori della Lazio di Gattuso festeggiano, ed è giusto che sia così. Quelli del Napoli di Allegri, invece, se la prendono con tutti, a cominciare dall’allenatore, per arrivare a quello che sembra essere diventato l’imputato numero uno. Imputato di che cosa, poi, non si capisce bene. Pensate che Noa Lang, da un certo momento in avanti, è stato fischiato per tutta la partita. Eppure Noa Lang è stato nettamente il migliore in campo del Napoli. Un giocatore vivo, sempre pronto a puntare l’uomo. Romano Floriani Mussolini, alla sua prima presenza da titolare, ha vissuto una giornata difficilissima, tanto da essere sostituito da Lazzari, perché nessuno riusciva a fermare Lang. Eppure i tifosi del Napoli lo fischiavano. Per che cosa? Per un gesto? Per una sorta di regolamento di conti? Non si capisce. Credo sia stato qualcosa che non dovrebbe trovare spazio nel giudizio su Lang. Naturalmente i tifosi possono fare quello che vogliono, ma il rendimento di un calciatore di personalità, come lo è Lang, un folle ma dotato di personalità, non dipende certo dai fischi o dagli applausi. Il rendimento di un giocatore o di una squadra non dipende dagli applausi o dai fischi dello stadio. E la dimostrazione, per certi versi, arriva proprio dalla Lazio. Mi dispiace dirlo, perché la passione dei tifosi laziali, compresi quelli che non vanno allo stadio, è fuori discussione. Però la dimostrazione che il pubblico conta fino a un certo punto arriva proprio dalla stagione della Lazio, che gioca in uno stadio quasi deserto eppure è in testa al campionato. Una squadra che sembrava destinata a lottare per non retrocedere sta invece lottando per lo scudetto. Vedremo quali saranno gli altri risultati, ma una cosa è sicura: chi, dopo queste prime giornate e le prime due soste, esclude la Lazio dalla lotta scudetto, secondo me commette un errore. È una squadra cresciuta con Gattuso, così come è cresciuto lo stesso allenatore, tornato, secondo me, alla semplicità, alla razionalità, alla precisione, al lavoro e alla solidità del suo primo staff, senza tutte le confusioni dell’esperienza in Nazionale. Quindi complimenti alla Lazio, ma per una volta complimenti anche al Napoli. Nel Napoli, Milinkovic-Savic ha parato quello che doveva parare, poi è stato impallinato da Frattesi. Sul gol del primo tempo il pallone gli passa praticamente accanto alla faccia. Per il resto è stato preciso negli interventi. Beukema un po’ meglio rispetto alle precedenti esibizioni, anche se non ci voleva molto. Rrahmani si vede che sta tirando avanti, lottando nonostante una condizione fisica complicata e dolori che potrebbero anche metterlo in difficoltà. Eppure continua a combattere con grande leadership. Rafa Marín discreto. Aveva offerto qualcosa di meglio nel corso della stagione, ma la sua resta una prestazione sufficiente. Olivera corre più di tutti, soltanto che poi sbaglia più di tutti sotto porta. È un giocatore che, se andassimo a vedere gli xG di questo campionato, probabilmente scopriremmo essere andato vicino al gol diverse volte, anche con salvataggi sulla linea. Poverino, non riesce mai a trovare la soddisfazione della rete. Nel secondo tempo ha avuto un pallone da calciare con il destro, che non è il suo piede. Era quasi un rigore, leggermente decentrato, ma lo ha mandato oltre la traversa. McTominay molto bene nel secondo tempo, così come De Bruyne, soprattutto quando i due si sono invertiti di posizione. Gilmour geometrico, didascalico e niente più. Vergara è partito molto male, ma ha concluso meglio. A me piace anche senza i gol, perché è un giocatore che, quando troverà maggiore fiducia, autostima e leggerezza mentale, potrà diventare molto più incisivo. E poi c’è Lang. È un giocatore che può dividere. Può risultare simpatico o, più probabilmente, antipatico. Può essere considerato un professionista serio, anche se non credo sia questa l’immagine che trasmette, oppure un folle, uno scapestrato, un genialoide, un artista, un rapper. Può essere considerato tutto. Ma se i tifosi del Napoli fischiano Lang per aver fatto quel gesto, significa che la competenza calcistica viene superata dall’umore, dall’invidia o da qualcosa che non ha nulla a che fare con il calcio e, se posso permettermi, nemmeno con il sostegno di cui questa squadra ha bisogno. Lo dico per i tifosi del Napoli, ma anche per quelli dell’Inter, della Roma, per quelli che l’anno scorso contestavano le proprie squadre e per quelli della Fiorentina. Se si va allo stadio concentrandosi sul fischiare un giocatore e sul trovare un capro espiatorio, come è successo anche a Lucca nell’ultimo quarto d’ora, va bene, si può fare tutto. I tifosi ne hanno il diritto, ma l’appoggio è un’altra cosa. Ed è proprio l’appoggio che i tifosi dovrebbero dare. Per me Lang è un giocatore di livello internazionale. È ovvio che non giocherà tutte le partite come questa, ma le sue qualità non si discutono. Concludendo, la Lazio è in corsa per lo scudetto. Il Napoli, se dovesse continuare a giocare così, potrebbe tornare a lottare per un posto tra le prime quattro. Ma deve continuare su questa strada”.

#2235. Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

Arsenal: Kepa (Meslier 46); White (Julienne 78), Mosquera (Ogunnaike 78), Gabriel (Salmon 60), Calafiori (Hincapié 60); Lewis-Skelly (Vieira 78), Havertz (O’Neill 78), Odegaard (Nwaneri 33); Dowman (Ibrahim 78), Gyokeres (Jesus 78), Tzolis (Martinielli 78). Substitutes: Setford, Nelson, Kabia.Booked: Gabriel.Goals: Nwaneri (54), Gyokeres (69 pen).Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson (Yamamoto 91), Inácio (Prates 59), Bensebaini (Reggiani 78), Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha (Guirassy 60), Mane; Karetsas (Chukwuemeka 46), Beier (Sabitzer 59), Silva (Albert 59). Substitutes: Drewes, Lerema, Kabar, Riedl.Goals: Inácio (7), Karetsas (29), Gadou (58).

Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

Meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

Another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

Arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:

With just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

The Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

In the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

During half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

Konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o

The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

Gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

After Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

Tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

With it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

Odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

The German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,

Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Odegaard; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.Substitutes: Meslier, Setford, Hincapie, Jesus, Martinielli, Vieira, Nwaneri, Nelson, Ibrahim, Kabia, Ogunnaike, Julienne, O’Neill, Salmon.

Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson, Inacio, Bensebaini, Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha, Mane; Karetsas, Beier, Silva.Substitutes: Drewes, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Sabitzer, Lerema, Prates, Albert, Kabar, Yamamoto, Reggiani, Riedl.

Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

Arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Odegaard; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.Substitutes: Meslier, Setford, Hincapie, Jesus, Martinielli, Vieira, Nwaneri, Nelson, Ibrahim, Kabia, Ogunnaike, Julienne, O’Neill, Salmon.

Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson, Inacio, Bensebaini, Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha, Mane; Karetsas, Beier, Silva.Substitutes: Drewes, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Sabitzer, Lerema, Prates, Albert, Kabar, Yamamoto, Reggiani, Riedl.

INS:Illan Meslier from Leeds, FreeChristos Tzolis from Club Brugge, £34mBruno Guimaraes from Newcastle, £75m

Piero Hincapie’s move from Bayer Leverkusen was made permanent this summer.

Checking in for the Emirates Cup 🛬 pic.twitter.com/mQ1eAESKHY

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

#2234. Lazio, Isaksen: «Sento la fiducia di Gattuso!» e la libertà in campo

Dal ritiro con la Danimarca, l’esterno descrive un tecnico che carica il gruppo e lavora con entusiasmo.

Gustav Isaksen sente la fiducia di Gattuso. L’esterno della Lazio, in ritiro con la Danimarca per le sfide di Nations League, descrive così il rapporto con il tecnico: «Sento la fiducia di Gattuso! E’ un tecnico che carica il gruppo e lavora con entusiasmo». Le sue parole, riportate da Laziochannel, arrivano in un momento di particolare fiducia per il giocatore.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Nel racconto del suo momento alla Lazio trova spazio anche la dimensione tattica. Isaksen percepisce la libertà di movimento come parte del proprio ruolo offensivo, in un contesto in cui questa possibilità convive con la chiarezza dei compiti in campo.

La guida di Gattuso viene associata all’energia e alla rapida integrazione tra i reparti. Sono aspetti che, nella lettura proposta dal resoconto, accompagnano il lavoro dell’esterno e contribuiscono alla crescita collettiva del gruppo.

La dichiarazione di Isaksen riguarda anche il modo in cui Gattuso lavora con la squadra. Il danese sottolinea la capacità dell’allenatore di caricare il gruppo e l’entusiasmo con cui svolge il suo lavoro. Il rapporto tra i due si inserisce così in un clima di fiducia che coinvolge lo spogliatoio.

#2233. Lo Monaco: "Napoli, a gennaio devi farti due domande. Mi mangio le mani per 3 giocatori"

"I mercati non sono quelli che cominciano e finiscono nei tempi canonici". A Radio Napoli Centrale parla così Pietro Lo Monaco, commentando presente e futuro della squadra partenopea: "A gennaio, la domanda che si deve porre il Napoli è sulla situazione generale: la rifondazione che doveva cominciare in estate, la vogliamo far partire a gennaio? La si vuole dividere in due tranche e completarla in estate? Sono domande alle quali vanno date risposte".

"Il Napoli ha bisogno di rivitalizzare la rosa. A centrocampo hai Anguissa, ma andrà via perché in scadenza e a questo punto ci vuole anche un atto di coraggio, magari una risoluzione. Mi mangio le mani per Cisse, Liberali, Doumbia. Tanti giocatori potevano essere presi a prezzi accessibili. Non per forza devi sempre vincere, certe volte ci sta che certi giocatori hanno chiuso e fatto il loro tempo. E se non ci sono richieste, vanno comunque mandati da qualche parte. Lucca per esempio se la fa addosso, è un ectoplasma. Ogni volta che va in possesso palla, tende ad andare sempre a terra. Ha paura. La maglia del Napoli pesa per lui, sarebbe disumano.

"Lang è un altro giocatore che difficilmente darà più di questo. Rafa Marin è un ripescato, era stato già bocciato. Se si considerano i soldi spesi per Lucca, Beukema, Lang, sono cento milioni: ma quanti se ne recuperano? Lang ad esempio in ammortamento può essere venduto a 15 milioni di euro. Le domande te le devi porre, ma devi anche darti risposte. E devi prendere decisioni"

#2232. EFL expert drops ‘exciting’ West Brom promotion prediction

West Brom are positioned in 5th place in the Championship table after 15 fixtures and are in the play-offs along with Stoke City, Wolves, Swansea City, Southampton and QPR. WBA are only a point behind joint-top Birmingham City and Middlesbrough.

The Baggies beat Millwall 3-0 at The Hawthorns last time out before the international break. Isaac Price, Jayson Molumby and Felix Horn Myhre got their goals against the Lions as they secured another eye-catching win.

Elek has been impressed with the Midlands outfit and has delivered his verdict on the latest episode of the Not The 20 Podcast on YouTube: “They have been absolutely phenomenal in the past couple of games. They’ve gone from a team I thought are going to start well and then drop off to a relegation scrap. They’ve proven me completely wrong. In 5th place, a point off top spot. Talking about can Birmingham maintain this, can West Brom? The answer is yes. The numbers are good, the performances are good. The results are good. The players are good. It’s all looking quite exciting.”

West Brom endured a tough past campaign and churned through both Ryan Mason and Eric Ramsay before they settled on James Morrison. WBA were in a relegation battle before Morrison managed to keep them up in the end.

Morrison has managed to steady the ship with the Baggies and has done a solid job. His side are now in the top eight and are eyeing the Premier League.

It was a busy summer for them and they ended up bringing in the likes of Jimmy-Jay Morgan, Barney Stewart and Rabby Nzingoula, among others, to bolster their ranks. They also cut ties with players including Alex Mowatt, Jed Wallace and Karlan Grant to help free up space and funds to pave the way for reinforcements.

West Brom opted to go for young and hungry players in the last transfer window and they now have a nice blend of youth and experience at their diposal. Morrison will get the opportunity to sign some more new faces in January if needed ahead of the second-half of this term.

As Elek has alluded to, West Brom should be considered genuine promotion contenders. WBA are solid at the back and have threats at the top end of the pitch.

In goalkeeper Max O’Leary, they have an experienced stopper who knows the league well and is a safe pair of hands. Defender George Campbell has become one of their most prized assets in defence alongside the know-how of Nat Phillips and/or Chris Mepham.

Nzingoula, Molumby and Ousmane Diakite have bags of energy in the middle of the park, whilst Horn Myhre and Price have quality to hurt opposition defenders. Up top, Morgan has a very bright future ahead of him in the game and the Baggies’ decision to sign him earlier this year was a masterstroke.

West Brom are back in action on Saturday 21st October with an away trip to Swansea City. They should be in confident mood ahead of their trek down to South Wales.

#2229. Carpi, in panchina ecco Miramari: "Una squadra e una città con storia e prestigio"

Dopo l'esonero di Stefano Cassani, annunciato circa un'ora fa, il Carpi rende noto anche il nuovo trainer: i biancorossi ripartono dall'ex Forlì Alessandro Miramari. Di seguito, la nota della società:

"L’AC Carpi rende noto di aver affidato l’incarico di Allenatore della Prima Squadra ad Alessandro Miramari. Contestualmente, la Società dà il benvenuto a Filippo Ceglia e Antonio Ciaccia, che assumeranno rispettivamente gli incarichi di Vice Allenatore e di Collaboratore Tecnico. Faranno ancora parte dello staff biancorosso i Preparatori Atletici, Graziano Araldi e Vito Barberio, e il Preparatore dei Portieri, Luca Malaguti.

Il nuovo staff dirigerà oggi pomeriggio – dalle ore 15:00 – il primo allenamento, presso l’Antistadio “Cabassi”".

Hanno poi fatto seguito le sue prime parole in biancorosso: "Di Carpi non c’è qualcosa che ti deve convincere. Quando parli di Carpi nel calcio parli di una squadra e di una città con storia e prestigio. Della Società mi hanno colpito subito entusiasmo e organizzazione, tipici della gente del nostro territorio. Mi sono sentito subito accolto in una famiglia. Adesso testa solo al campo, per ottenere i risultati che ci sono stati richiesti“.

#2228. FIGC, Galliani e Malagò davanti al TFN: voto del 14 dicembre a rischio

La Federazione si costituisce nel procedimento sulla commissione incaricata di controllare le candidature.

La FIGC ha deciso di costituirsi davanti al Tribunale Federale Nazionale nel procedimento avviato dal ricorso di Adriano Galliani contro la commissione nominata da Giovanni Malagò per verificare le candidature alla presidenza federale. Secondo quanto riportato da Onefootball, Il TFN ascolterà le parti prima di pronunciarsi collegialmente. La controversia potrebbe far slittare le elezioni, per ora fissate al 14 dicembre.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Secondo Onefootball, il calendario della procedura è già stretto: l’elenco dei candidati ammessi dovrebbe essere pubblicato entro il 14 novembre. Il limite stabilito dal CONI per celebrare l’assemblea elettiva resta il 31 gennaio 2027.

Galliani ha presentato il ricorso lunedì 9 novembre tramite il proprio legale, l’avvocato Filippo Lattanzi. L’atto riguarda la commissione istituita il 2 novembre da Malagò, commissario straordinario della FIGC e a sua volta candidato alla presidenza. All’organismo è stato affidato il controllo della regolarità delle candidature.

Per Galliani, la commissione non sarebbe prevista dalle norme statutarie e regolamentari della Federazione e non avrebbe quindi titolo per effettuare quelle verifiche. Il ricorso contesta anche la scelta di istituirla da parte di Malagò, direttamente coinvolto nella competizione elettorale.

La richiesta al TFN è di sospendere in via cautelare l’efficacia del provvedimento e poi annullarlo. Secondo la posizione sostenuta da Galliani, il controllo delle candidature dovrebbe essere svolto dagli organi già individuati dalle norme federali, in particolare dalla Segreteria generale e dal segretario Marco Brunelli. Galliani è sostenuto da Assocalciatori e Assoallenatori.

Nel confronto sulle candidature ha un peso anche la posizione del Genoa. In un primo momento l’amministratore delegato rossoblù Andres Blazquez aveva sottoscritto l’accredito a favore di Galliani. Successivamente il presidente Dan Sucu ha espresso il sostegno del club a Malagò, accompagnandolo con una comunicazione formale di revoca e diffida relativa alla precedente adesione.

Malagò ha presentato undici accrediti di club di Serie A, esattamente il minimo richiesto. Se quello del Genoa non fosse considerato valido, uno degli undici sostegni necessari verrebbe meno e la candidatura potrebbe non soddisfare il requisito previsto.

Il ricorso di Galliani, però, non chiede direttamente l’esclusione di Malagò. Il suo oggetto principale è la legittimità della commissione incaricata dei controlli. La posizione del Genoa resta un elemento del contenzioso e potrebbe assumere rilievo nella successiva valutazione dei requisiti.

#2227. The 3 summer targets Blackburn Rovers should pursue again in January, including Balazs Toth replacement

Blackburn Rovers have exceeded the expectations of many in the early stages of the 2026/27 campaign. Tony Mowbray‘s side sit 13th in the Championship after 15 games, when many expected them to be in the thick of a relegation battle.

That fate could yet await with a lot of the season left to play, but spirits are fairly high at Ewood Park. There is no hiding that the Rovers squad needs work though, with only three new summer signings failing to suitably reinforce the ranks.

New targets will be on the radar, but Blackburn Rovers identified some smart options in the summer who could be available this winter. Here, we put forward three summer targets who should be back on the radar ahead of January…

Balazs Toth has continued to resist Blackburn Rovers’ new contract efforts. It remains to be seen exactly when he leaves, but a departure seemingly awaits at some point in 2027, and the club could do with sourcing a replacement sooner rather than later.

Alex Palmer was linked with a move to Ewood Park in the last transfer window, and he could be a fine option to consider to replace Toth. The 30-year-old is out of favour at Ipswich Town under Gary O’Neil, but he is a proven Championship goalkeeper who could quickly become a dependable No. 1 for Mowbray.

Palmer is under contract until 2028 at Portman Road but given that he has not made a Premier League matchday squad this season, the Tractor Boys should not have an issue letting him go for a fairly cheap fee.

Blackburn Rovers have one of Europe’s most clinical strikers in Andri Gudjohnsen at the moment, but competition beyond him is limited. Yuki Ohashi is the only other out-and-out centre-forward, so more depth would not go amiss.

Daniel Jebbison was targeted by Rovers in the summer and a loan-to-buy deal was even agreed, but he ended up staying at Bournemouth. Given the fact that he has played only four times so far this season, the 23-year-old would benefit from a winter move elsewhere to find more game time.

The Canadian striker has Championship experience and has strong physical traits like Gudjohnsen. Jebbison is a strong finisher on both feet and Mowbray’s style of play and ability to develop players could help him hit prolific form.

Last but not least is a much-needed midfield reinforcement. Mowbray has expressed a desire to sign a new central midfielder in the winter, and someone who offers experience but has more years ahead of Sam Morsy and Adam Forshaw would be ideal.

Alan Browne fits this profile perfectly. The 31-year-old has played over 400 Championship games but showed on loan at Middlesbrough last season that he still has plenty in the tank, offering a well-rounded skillset, versatility and energy in the middle of the park.

Browne is way down the pecking order at Sunderland and out of contract next summer. It should be an easy deal for Blackburn Rovers to strike and he would instantly improve their options in midfield.

#2226. Ndour, Calvani e Cichella lasciano il raduno dell'U21. Anche Vavassori escluso dalla convocazione

Quattro defezioni nella Nazionale Under 21, che dopo l'allenamento della mattina tornerà in campo nel pomeriggio per la seduta di allenamento. Non saranno infatti presenti i giocatori del Frosinone Gabriele Calvani e Matteo Cichella, così come il centrocampista della Fiorentina Cher Ndour: valutati indisponibili, i tre hanno lasciato il ritiro del CPO di Tirrenia facendo ritorno ai rispettivi club. Anche Dominic Vavassori del Palermo, a seguito della valutazione del quadro influenzale dei giorni scorsi, è stato escluso dalla convocazione.

Restano pertanto ventiquattro i calciatori a disposizione di Baldini in vista delle amichevoli con Francia e Belgio in programma venerdì 13 (alle 18.30 a Laval) e lunedì 16 (all’Armando Picchi di Livorno alle 18.15). Fra questi c’è Matteo Dagasso, assente dalle convocazioni di ottobre per infortunio, che ha ritrovato gli Azzurrini dopo aver festeggiato, seppur da lontano, la qualificazione alla fase finale dell’Europeo nella ‘sua’ Pescara. “Il nostro obiettivo era qualificarci, ci abbiamo lavorato molto fin dal primo raduno. Si è creato un grandissimo gruppo e questa alchimia fra di noi ci ha portato a raggiungere il pass per la fase finale”. Il 26 l’Italia scoprirà le sue avversarie ad Albania e Serbia 2027: “Ci penseremo più avanti, ora siamo concentrati su queste due importanti amichevoli”.

Portieri: Giovanni Daffara (Parma), Diego Mascardi (Torino), Lorenzo Palmisani (Frosinone), Massimo Pessina (Bologna); Difensori: Davide Bartesaghi (Milan), Fabio Chiarodia (Borussia M’Gladbach), Pietro Comuzzo (Torino), Eddy Kouadio (Monza), Emanuele Lulli (Roma), Filippo Mane (Borussia Dortmund), Brando Moruzzi (Avellino); Centrocampisti: Lorenzo Amatucci (Deportivo La Coruna), Tommaso Berti (Cremonese), Matteo Dagasso (Venezia), Giacomo Faticanti (Avellino), Luca Lipani (Sassuolo), Mattia Mannini (Benevento); Attaccanti: Alessio Cacciamani (Torino), Francesco Camarda (Milan), Luigi Cherubini (Benevento), Jeff Ekhator (Juventus), Seydou Fini (Frosinone), Samuele Inacio (Borussia Dortmund).
